chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله used to detain in a blood accusation for six days; then if the heirs of the slain came with a proof that established it, otherwise he would let them go.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءُ: the heirs or legal claimants of the slain person
key_terms.بَيِّنَةٍ: a clear legal proof or evidence
key_terms.خَلَّى سَبِيلَهُمْ: released them and let them go free

ai.seo_question: How long could a person be detained in a murder accusation according to this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith states that in cases of accusation involving bloodshed, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله would detain the accused for six days while awaiting proof from the slain person’s heirs. If conclusive evidence was brought, the claim proceeded; otherwise, the accused were released.
